ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=45^\circ$, D is a point on BC, $\angle ADC=60^\circ$, $AE\perp BC$ at point E, $CF\perp AD$ at point F, $AE$ and $CF$ intersect at point G, $\angle CAE=15^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle ACF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because \angle ADC=60^\circ$ and $AE \perp BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAE=30^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle CAE=15^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CAF=\angle CAE+\angle DAE=45^\circ$,\\
$\because CF \perp AD$,\\
$\therefore \angle ACF=90^\circ-\angle CAF=45^\circ$.

Thus, the answer is $\angle ACF=\boxed{45^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows triangle ABC with B and C on a horizontal base BC and A above the base. Points D and E lie on BC, with E between D and C. Segment AE is drawn vertically from A down to E, indicating AE is perpendicular to BC. Segment AD is a slanted line from A down to D, and point F lies on AD. Segment CF is drawn from C to F and intersects AE at G; the figure indicates CF is perpendicular to AD at F. The ray AE lies between rays AD and AC at vertex A. Reasoning: Since D and C are both on the base BC, ray DC lies along BC. Given ∠ADC = 60° and AE ⟂ BC, the angle between AD and AE is 90° − 60° = 30°, so ∠DAE = 30°. Given ∠CAE = 15°, and AE lies between AD and AC, we have ∠CAF = ∠CAE + ∠EAD = 15° + 30° = 45° because F lies on AD. Since CF ⟂ AD and F lies on AD, triangle ACF is right-angled at F. Therefore ∠ACF = 90° − ∠CAF = 90° − 45° = 45°.
